blind.why: FP run strips (ours: real map open lane, 30 fps; CS2 trailer_1 37.9s). Both cameras rock-steady (phase-correlation shift 0-1 px/frame), but CS2 strip reads as purposeful motion via weapon sway and travel; ours looks near-static frame to frame. Running FOV kick (+1 deg vertical) is invisible in practice.

Normalized speed and jump charts vs a CS2 Source-constant model. Ours reaches 90% speed in 0.15 s (CS2 about 0.45 s) and stops on a counter-strafe in 0.08 s; release stop matches CS2 at 0.42 s. Hop is shorter and snappier (0.60 s vs 0.76 s). A 100 ms CS-habit tap overshoots to -13% (still accurate).

Strafe-jump gain with identical scripted inputs at 4 turn rates. Ours gains about 0.3 m/s per hop up to a soft cap of about 1.26-1.3x run, which suits a 5v5. The idealized Source curve is unbounded. Ours shows small speed notches at each landing.

biggest_gap: Wedge phantom velocity. On the movement course, goto('vcrease') and hold W for 2 s. The player wedges in the 30-degree V and stays wedged. actor.move.speed reads 0.62 m/s indefinitely, the position oscillates on a 3-tick cycle (about 2 mm), and a footstep event fires every 0.31 s while the player is stationary (5 in 2 s). Enemies would hear footsteps from a player who is not moving. Real-map fuzz also produced momentary phantom speed of 4.03 m/s with 0.05 m/s actual displacement at (-12.45,1.4,39.99). CS2 reports zero velocity once blocked and emits no steps. Fix: derive speed and footsteps from post-collision displacement, and settle the crease with a multi-plane clip (2-plane crease gives a velocity along the crease line, 3+ planes gives zero).
other_gaps: Stair-top snag. On goto('stairs44') (0.44 m rise) at full run, speed collapses from 6.6 to 0.9 m/s at the landing lip (about tick 110), then takes 0.25 s to recover. stairs18, stairs30 and stairsFine are clean.

Bhop landing notches. Each landing visibly drops speed even with buffered jumps, so chains feel sawtoothed rather than fluid. With a soft cap already in place, perfect-timing landings should not also lose speed.

Run camera conveys little speed: about 1.6 cm vertical bob, 0.2 degree roll and +1 degree FOV. Per eye height, 6.6 m/s at a 1.62 m eye is about 4.1 eye-heights/s against CS2's 3.9, so the run is effectively CS2 pace, not 'faster'.
Slide is modest: x1.14 boost, 0.9 s, 2.6 degree roll and +1.5 degree FOV. It reads as a crouch-dip more than a burst.
Speed-dependent FOV kick shifts on-screen target size between moving and stationary. CS2 keeps FOV fixed. Make it optional or remove it.
No crouch-jump height bonus (peak 1.053 m either way). CS players expect +about 9 u. Mantle covers boxes up to 1.4 m, but 1.5 m fails.
bugs: vcrease: phantom speed 0.62 m/s and footstep events every 0.31 s while wedged, with 3-tick position jitter.
stairs44: speed collapses from 6.6 to 0.9 m/s at the top step.
Real map: momentary phantom speed of 4.03 m/s while blocked near (-12.45,1.4,39.99).
strengths: Real-map nav routes (9 spawn/site routes, about 70 s total) had no snags, no airtime on stairs and no camera jerk over 3 cm.
24-episode real-map fuzz had no NaN, no fall-through and no tunnelling. The 40 m/s thin-wall test held.
Sensitivity is exactly CS (1000 counts = 22 degrees) and pitch is clamped at +/-89.
Coyote time works up to about 8 ticks and jump buffering up to about 10 ticks. Mantle works up to 1.4 m.
Counter-strafe is crisp: accurate in 0.05 s.
Landing dip is 10 cm with recovery in about 0.25 s. Stair camera smoothing works. A 30-degree wall slide keeps full speed.
